reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 29-40 feet on jigs and minnows.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows and jigs moving deeper midday. Topwater bass action has started. Most bass are 8-15 inches being caught on slow moving plastics. Report by Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide.
reports.by: Shon Riley, Lake Amistad Fishing Guides

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has become tougher as the Texas heat sets in.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early morning chasing shad off the deep channels onto the flats.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with soft plastics and crankbaits.
reports.by: Hundley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are feeding on the abundant shad schools and can be found at freshwater inlets. The Crappie bite has been light all week but they are still being caught over bush and on timber. Roaming Crappie have been feeding aggressively. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Check out the backs of coves for hydrilla and milfoil, fish patterns should draw bass out from cover. Crappie are excellent for big fish and numbers on brush piles, or timber in 10-30 feet of water on main river channels.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Early morning bass bite has picked up around shad spawning areas with topwater lures. Crappie are excellent on brush piles, near the bridge, and the back of coves. Crappie will not be on locust trees due to the thorns.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are primarily roaming but finding some active fish on dock poles or brush. Largemouth bass bite is decent in shallow water using topwaters and crankbaits. White bass and hybrids are good on main lake humps with slabs or live shad. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 7.47 pounds are good in 8-18 feet of water on wacky rigged Hag’s Jigs or Tornados, topwaters and spinnerbaits. Bass have finished guarding fry and have moved into an early summer pattern. Crappie are excellent with catches up to 15 inches on minnows and jigs in 18-25 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: White bass continue to bite on slabs and soft plastics 20-36 feet of water on wind-blown points and humps. Lake Buchanan is still producing numbers of largemouth bass, stripers and white bass/hybrids in 5-15 feet of water. A swimbait and crankbait or catching most of these and you'll find schooling fish all over the lake, especially on flats near deep water as the bass push shad shallow.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and freshwater drum on shrimp and cropping with a variety of colors.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been good on points and structure as well as bream beds. Crappie are fair on brush from 10-25 feet. Hybrids and white bass are on flats and drop-offs in 14-26 feet of water using live large goldfish or minnows, slabs, spoons, and crankbaits.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in a full post spawn pattern in 8-16 feet of water on timber, and on the south end in brush piles.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with underspins, rattle traps and spinnerbaits in less than 4 feet of water. Still waiting for bass to start suspending.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Target bass feeding on the shad early in the morning with square bill crankbaits, chatterbaits, spinnerbaits, and topwaters. Fish this type of cover at mid day when bass are seeking cover. Drop a clouser on isolated cover for black bass. Crappie fishing on Lake Fork is a lot of fun right now. The lake has a tremendous population of black crappie and they are stacked up on all kinds of structures all over the lake in 12-28 feet. White crappie are also loading up on certain trees. You can find black crappie on some bridges, underwater bridges, roadbeds, brush piles, lay downs, tire reefs, points and the base of timber. I have seen some lay downs the past week that may have over 1000 crappie…
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Bigger striped bass are being taken on 1 ounce slabs and live shad fished mainly on the lower ends from Decordova to near the pump stations close to the dam. Smaller stripers and sand bass are easily being caught on slabs and spinnerbaits all over the lake from Bentwater to Blue Water Shores. Largemouth bass are good to 6 pounds on soft plastics and lipless crankbaits fished in the back of sloughs and near main lake points. Crappies are holdings to structure near deeper docks, underwater timber and near bridge pilings and are good on small minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good in shallow water early morning with spinnerbaits, then in deep water with slabs.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Topwater lures early and late will produce good black bass action.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Water is starting to clear up nicely making for a decent largemouth bite in the shallows. Crappie are picking up quite a bit in Luces Bayou, tight to structure being enticed with minnows and hand tied jigs in 6-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on brush from 6-20 feet on soft plastics and swimbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is in a post spawn funk. Crappie are still in the timber on minnows, but you have to hit several spots.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on offshore structure in 12-17 feet. Crappie are good on slip cork jigs around standing timber.
reports.by: Brian Vickery Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair to good on points and humps in 15-32 feet of water with jigs, slabs, and live bait. Crappie are slow to fair in 8-28 feet of water on brush piles, submerged timber, and submerged cover near drop-offs with minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are moving to offshore brush piles in 10-20 feet of water on minnows. Largemouth bass are in 2-7 feet of water on Texas rigs, chatterbaits, and topwater frogs.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good targeting the hydrilla with swimbaits and Texas rigged worms. Crappie are schooled up on brush piles in 25 feet of water with minnows.
reports.by: Hambone guide service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are starting to stack deeper in the brush piles with jigs or minnows.
reports.by: Navarro Mills Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on long tapering points 8-18 feet of water with red bug or plum Texas rigged 10 inch worms. Crappie fishing is improving on big timber suspended midlake around the old Leaday or Cemetery area. Reports of crappie on minnows working best.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and largemouth bass have been slow.
reports.by: Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are fair to slow in 15-25 feet of water on main lake points with small slabs, white and silver are both good colors.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on weedless rigged artificial worms in red-tinted colors with glitter. No reports of crappie or catfish in recent weeks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are relating to brush piles 15-20 feet of water. Crappie are showing up at bridge columns and they are moving around drop off going from structure to structure.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in a summer pattern on brush piles in 25-30 feet of water, or on timber in 14-24 feet of water with natural colored jigs and minnows. Bass are on main lake points and secondary points near dropoffs or deep timber hitting topwaters or crankbaits jigs and 10 inch worms. Sand bass are on mainlake humps and points chasing bait fish in deep water with live bait and slabs. Dan’s Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan’s Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: A slab and jig combination is hard to beat. Crappie action is slow. Black bass fishing is fair and the water is stained. This along with the brim will keep some bass shallow.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Numbers of bass are shallow in the buckbrush, so flip plastics and jigs. Target bass on points and drains with crankbaits, or with jigs and Carolina rigs off ledges and structure. Crappie are slowly move out to brush and timber.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with the best bite in shallow water with topwaters, swim jigs and frogs. Crappie fishing is fair in shallow brush piles and standing timber all with live bait is the best.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are great and on the chew all over the lake. There is good schooling bass action in the marinas about a half hour before sunrise. The bass are eating like crazy at sunrise. Bass are still on bluff walls.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles with minnows and jigs in 10-16 feet of water. Bass are fair on trick worms, spinnerbaits and topwaters. Bass are in a full post spawn, targeting fry balls for aggressive strikes is producing well right now. Schooling crappie are good in 12-20 feet of water on brush. Individual large crappie are still able to be caught under boat houses if you can reach them.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie spawn is over and fish have transitioned to a summer pattern relating to brush in 10-18 feet of water. Black bass up to 8 pounds are suspended over structure in 20 feet of water hitting crankbaits or a silver spoon. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 10-20 feet of water on brush piles with minnows and jigs. Bass are slow on soft plastics in deeper water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on main lake brush piles in 15-30 feet of water. White bass fishing is good on slabs on main lake humps in 25-30 feet of water. Largemouth bass fishing is good using soft plastics on deep structure.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are loading up on timber, or brush piles in 10-20 feet of water. Crappie are moving into brush piles and structure setting up in a summer pattern.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 18-39 feet on jigs and minnows.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Crappie great on minnows and jigs in mouths of coves, moving deeper mid day, great under lights near docks and structure at night. Report by Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide.
reports.by: Shon Riley, Lake Amistad Fishing Guides

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in grass 8-12 feet of water with Texas rig worms, wacky rig senko and crankbaits. Crappie are slow on small jigs over brush. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good working the discharge early and often will get bites with small swimbaits, worms and crankbaits. Bass are schooling offshore in the main lake hitting clear topwaters, shad colored squarebill crankbaits, or Alabama rigs rolled extremely slow off the bottom. Some bass can still be caught early and late in the day in the reeds and grass.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth bass can still be caught on rocky points with crankbaits and Texas rigs. Largemouth bass males are guarding fry so still kinda easy to catch on any flooded brush.
reports.by: Hundley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are setting in 5-10 feet staging to run in on spawning shad and bluegill. Crappie are getting into summer patterns with large numbers loading up on brush and the larger fish suspended on the deeper timber. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Black bass are shallow in creeks and shallow banks. Fly fishing with craws and clouser minnow patterns should produce bass. Crappie and catfish are moving shallow fly fishing with wooly buggers, slow-sinking small fish patterns, or clouser minnows on sunny rocky shores might draw a strike. Crappie are excellent for big fish and numbers on brush piles, or timber in 10-30 feet of water on main river channels.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: The morning bass bite is slow, but buzz baits and ribbits will land fish around any flooded weeds or pond weeds. Crappie are excellent on brush piles, near the bridge, and the back of coves. Crappie will not be on locust trees due to the thorns.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are primarily roaming, but there are some active fish on dock poles. Largemouth bass are slow shallow using topwaters and chatterbaits. White bass and hybrids are good on wind blown points with crankbaits and main lake humps, slabs or live shad. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 4.47 pounds are good in 3-15 feet of water on wacky rigged Hag’s Tornados, topwaters and spinnerbaits. Some bass are guarding fry and the rest are in an early summer pattern. Crappie are slow to 13 inches on jigs in 12-25 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: White bass continue to bite well on slabs and soft plastics 20-36 feet of water on wind-blown points and humps. Crappie are good on brush in 25 feet. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good, feeding on points and rock piles in 5-12 feet of water.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: There are some schooling bass in the lake, and some white bass are running in the river. The bass will continue to hold tight to the trees as the lake falls. The bass cannot resist a pop r when they are focused on bream.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Black bass slow, some caught in the cattails.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Black bass caught off the bank with plastics and spinner baits 3-5 pounds.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 8-10 feet of water with soft plastics worms, craw worms and lizards on reeds and stumps.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are active early and late on the edges, then move to rocks and docks. Crappie are fair on jigs and minnows in 10–25 feet around structure. Hybrids and white bass are on flats and drop-offs in 14-26 feet of water using live large goldfish or minnows, slabs, spoons, and crankbaits.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in a full postspawn pattern in 8-16 feet of water on timber, and on the south end in brush piles.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good early morning on timber. Black bass are cruising in 10-15 feet in creek channels and around timber chasing shad. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Crappie are congregating on boat docks and brush piles.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and sand bass are slow due to the muddy water. Reports of largemouth bass being caught up to 8 pounds.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with rattle traps, spinnerbaits and underspins on shallow points in 3 feet of water following fish to 17-20 feet of water as the day progresses.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the early morning on points where the shad are spawning. Black bass are post spawn and the top water bite is on! The crappie are moving shallow, small clousers are producing well. Crappie fishing on Lake Fork is a lot of fun right now. The lake has a tremendous population of black crappie and they are stacked up on all kinds of structures all over the lake in 12-28 feet. White crappie are also loading up on certain trees. You can find black crappie on some bridges, underwater bridges, roadbeds, brush piles, lay downs, tire reefs, points and the base of timber. I’ve seen some lay downs the past week that may have over 1000 crappie on them. The only problem is finding black…
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is slow. Bass are in shallow water feeding on shad. Crappie fishing is slow on brush piles in 14 feet of water with minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass action continues to be good to excellent on slabs and spinner baits on many areas of the lake. Largemouth bass are good on soft plastics and lipless crankbaits worked in the back of sloughs and creeks. Some largemouth bass are schooling with the sand bass. Crappie reports are also good in the creeks on small minnows and jigs. Some of the crappies are moving out to structure near major creek entrances and near bridge pilings and standing timber.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair to 6 pounds on white spinnerbaits. Crappie are good on jigs fished in brush piles all over the lake.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Numbers of white bass can be caught on jigging spoons and slabs utilizing a thumper to bring fish beneath the boat.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: The largemouth bass bite has dwindled on the backside of the full moon. Bass are shallow feeding up in the grass, so there is a small window for topwaters in the early morning. Crappie are very tight to structure in 6-10 feet of water eating minnows, but you almost have to thump them in the head to get them to eat.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Inks fishing report
reports.text: Inks Lake has been fishing well all year for bass.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting soft plastics and jigs on brush and humps in 8-16 feet. Suspended bass on brush are biting swimbaits and jerkbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early on shad pattern crankbaits, 8-10 inch Texas rig worms on isolated cover.
reports.by: Brian Vickery Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 2-4 feet of water jigging trees and bushes, or on main lake structure in 7-10 feet. When sandies are on top throw paddle tail swimbaits, otherwise target 15-30 feet of water after 8 a.m. with 1 ounce minnow slab.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 18-24 feet of water with jigs and minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good on docks and bulkheads in 3-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair to good on points and humps in 15-32 feet of water with jigs, slabs, and live bait. Crappie are slow to fair in 2-24 feet of water on brush piles, submerged timber, and submerged cover near drop-offs with minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on wacky worms around the hydrilla in 8-10 feet of water. Crappie are good suspended in brush piles using minnows and pintail jigs.
reports.by: Hambone guide service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are starting to stack deeper in the brush piles and mostly wanting minnows. Off the banks and docks some crappie and white bass are still being caught.
reports.by: Navarro Mills Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass good to 12 pounds scoping 8-18 feet of water. Crappie are slow with very few reports.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting in 6 feet of water.
reports.by: Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are relating to brush piles in 15-20 feet of water. Crappie are showing up at bridge columns and they are moving around drop off going from structure to structure.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are almost in a full swing summer pattern in 10-25 feet of water on brush piles hitting minnows. Largemouth bass can be caught on windblown points chasing bait or shallow brush. White bass are on main lake humps with slabs, rattle traps or live shad. Catfish and largemouth bass can also be caught under the white bass. Dan’s Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan’s Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: A slab and jig combination is best, but MAL Lures, Mepps Spinners, and Lil' Georges are good. Hybrid stripers are good with live shad, or bumping slabs off the bottom near the 309 Flats and Pelican Island. Crappie action is slow. Black Bass fishing is fair at this time.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the Marina the crappie bite is fair, and the catfish are fair on minnows or punch bait. Crappie are fair on jigs and minnows over brush in 8-18 feet of water. Black bass are good on crankbaits and shiny spinnerbaits in 2-8 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Shallow bass bite is good with frogs, topwaters and swimbaits around the flooded bushes and hay grass. Bass are showing up in 12-18 feet on Texas and Carolina rigged big worms, with a few coming on crankbaits. Crappie are fair in 10-16 feet of water on standing timber or brush. Most of all the crappie are out of creeks and off the grass.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on the grass flats in the mid and lower part of the lake. Bass are also setup on points, ledges and docks. Bass are excellent around hydrilla and grass with big topwaters and shad colored swimbaits on shallow grass, and green pumpkin or watermelon baby brush hogs and flukes along the edge of grass.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles with minnows in 10-16 feet of water. Bass are good on trick worms, spinnerbaits and topwater. Bass are in a full post spawn, targeting fry balls for aggressive strikes is producing well right now. Schooling crappie are good in 12-20 feet of water on brush. Individual large crappie are still able to be caught under boat houses if you can reach them.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 10-20 feet of water on brush piles with minnows and jigs. Bass are slow to fair on soft plastics in deeper water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Crappie great on minnows and jigs in mouths of coves, moving deeper mid day, great under lights near docks and structure at night. Bass can also be caught with 3-5 inch swimbaits on the same flats, or in areas with small depth changes in 5-15 feet of water. Report by Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide.
reports.by: Shon Riley, Lake Amistad Fishing Guides

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good working small topwaters on top of grass. Forward facing sonar and a minnow style bait have been catching bass suspended out around bait.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good working the discharge early and often will get bites with small swimbaits, worms and crankbaits. Bass are primarily schooling midday offshore in the main lake. Some bass can still be caught early and late in the day in the reeds and grass.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good early morning on timber. Black bass are cruising in 10-15 feet in creek channels and around timber chasing shad. Report by Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide. Black bass are shallow in creeks and shallow banks. Fly fishing with craws and clouser minnow patterns should produce bass. Crappie and catfish are moving shallow fly fishing with wooly buggers, slow-sinking small fish patterns, or clouser minnows on sunny rocky shores might draw a strike. Crappie are excellent in timber and coves in 10-20 feet of water with jigs out producing minnows.
reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Morning bass bite has been slow but should pick up soon. Crappie are excellent despite the rise in water the clarity is still good.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good fishing around reed lines with dark colored plastics.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are scattered and the bite is slow. Largemouth bass are fair on shallow structure using white spinnerbaits and chatterbaits. Report by Jack Pelligrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pelligrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 5.25 pounds are slow in 3-15 feet of water on Hag’s Tornados, topwaters and spinnerbaits. Some bass are post spawn and a few are into an early summer pattern. Crappie are slow to 10 inches on jigs in 9-15 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Brush piles have been a huge factor to catch bass after the shad spawn. Bass can still be caught shallow, but offshore points and rock have produced the best.
reports.by: the Aggie Anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good around brush and timber in 15-20 feet of water with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good working rocks from the bank to 15 feet throwing swimbaits and crankbaits with any soft plastic to follow up with.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Tree bass are steady with senkos, flukes, Texas rig worms, tubes and craw worms. Seems like when the lake falls or rises the bass seem to hold even tighter to the trees.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Focus on using slabs on drop offs and along seawalls early in the mornings in depth of 5-14 feet. Reports of great catches using silver or white slabs and spinners and retrieving off the bottom at a very slow retrieve to catch these fish in depths of 17-26 feet of water. The crappie have also migrated back into the main lake.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Perch, channel catfish and bass are good in 8-30 feet of water with minnows and shrimp.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass continue to be good in 1-7 feet of water with soft plastics worms, craw worms and lizards on reeds and stumps.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on the edges early and late then on offshore structures midday. Crappie are fair on structure 8-25 feet of water with jigs and minnows. Hair jigs from Lone Star Crappie are outperforming plastics. Hybrids and whites can be caught with slabs, spoons, crankbaits, live large gold fish or live large minnows.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, with Bradley Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report

reports.text: Crappie are good early morning on timber. Black bass are cruising in 10-15 feet in creek channels and around timber chasing shad. reports.by: Chris Caswell, Lake Bob Sandlin Crappie Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: There is some bass action with topwaters, spinnerbaits and rattle traps very early before sunrise. Midday bass are good on the edge of points in 14-17 feet of water with shaky heads and Carolina rigged worms. Big bluegill can be caught on plastic worms while targeting bass.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair on points with and without spawning shad early morning. Bass are staging in 5-10 feet of water on secondary points hitting Carolina rigs, and XD 5-6. Black bass are post spawn and the top water bite is on! The crappie are moving shallow, small clousers are producing well. Crappie fishing is settling into the post spawn and summer patterns we should see for the next few months. We are seeing incredible numbers of small black crappie right now loading up on brush piles, lay downs, bridges and docks. The larger black crappie are a little hard to find but you can find some nice groups of them or pick a few out of the smaller fish. The bigger white crappie are beginning to load on…
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Sandbass are excellent on slabs and mepps spinners. Crappie continue to be caught in the back of creeks, but many are returning to structure on the main lake. Largemouth bass to 6lbs continue to be good in the back of the creeks in clearer water.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Target bass in clear water near shad with 5 inch worms Texas rigged. Crappie should be picking up at the end of next week when the water clarity improves in Luces Bayou and East Fork.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report

Crappie are fair on brush piles with minnows in 12-15 feet of water.

reports.text: White bass are good on points and humps in 15-32 feet of water with jigs, slabs, and live bait. Crappie are slow to fair in 2-24 feet of water on brush piles, submerged timber, and submerged cover near drop-offs with minnows and jigs.

reports.text: Crappie are slow in deep water.
reports.by: Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on small swimbaits or large swimbaits with fish suspended over grass. Crappie are fair on brush piles and near the pump house.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Use live shad or small white, silver or chrome slabs in 15-25 feet of water.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: A slab and jig combination is best, but MAL Lures, Mepps Spinners, and Lil' Georges are good. Crappie action is slow. Richland Chambers Black Bass fishing is fair to good.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the Marina the crappie bite is fair, bluegill are fair on crickets or worms, the catfish are fair on minnows or punch bait. Crappie are fair on jigs and minnows over brush in 8-18 feet of water. Black bass are good on crankbaits and shiny spinnerbaits in 2-8 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass and crappie continue to be tough.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Limits of striped bass are possible with slabs.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Shallow bass fishing is fair with topwaters, frogs and swim jigs. Mid range bass are fair 8-12 feet of water with Carolina rigs, Texas rigs and mid range crankbaits. Crappie do not like the flow and rising water so the bite is hit-or-miss.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass and white bass are biting throughout the lake on bluff walls and creeks. Bass are very good hungry after the spawn. Bass are excellent around hydrilla and grass with big topwaters and shad colored swimbaits on shallow grass, and green pumpkin or watermelon baby brush hogs and flukes along the edge of grass.
reports.by: Randal Frisbee, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 10-20 feet of water on brush piles with minnows and jigs. Bass are fair on soft plastics in deeper water. Bass and crappie spawn are over.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good 2-8 feet on jigs and minnows.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are pulling out of coves and the shallows migrating along main channels on timber in 14-17 feet of water. Smaller crappie are moving on brush, with bigger fish on timber biting quarter ounce Jigs with two plastics..
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 20-28 feet of water on minnows.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good up to 2 pounds with occasional 5-6 pounder. Crappie are good on crappie jigs and small cranks fished around wood.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arrowhead fishing report
reports.text: Crappie had moved out into the summer post spawning grounds.
reports.by: Brandon Brown, Brown’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Some bass still spawning in lake Austin around full moons.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been good on flukes and swimbaits in shad or bluegill colors. Report by Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop. Bass are biting early in the morning in the discharge on shaky heads and small Carolina rigged super fluke juniors. Later in the day bass are moving to grass lines on the main lake hitting using flukes, worms and creature baits. Schooling bass action on small swimbaits and tiny clear topwaters.
reports.by: Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in brush piles 20-25 feet with minnows or jigs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are good in 12-15 feet of water on points and brush piles with Texas rigged worms, jigging spoons, dropshots and jigs. Black bass are slow on streamers and clousers fishing main lake points and flooded grass.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: The top waters bass bite is slow in most areas, but a frog bite is working in other areas.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brady fishing report
reports.text: Black bass bite is spotty. Crappie and white bass are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to be good around shoreline cover, brush piles and the U.S. Chartreuse slabs will catch fish when they are under the boat. Try a topwater bait for early morning bass.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 7.71 pounds are slow on jigs, shaky heads and top waters in 2-10 feet. Crappie to 13 inches are excellent under docks on minnows in 6-12 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on spooks in the morning. Then as the sun rises target bass around grass edges with worms.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bass morning bite is really good on shad patterned spinnerbaits or crankbaits. Bass are good in shallow water out to 10 feet using flukes and soft plastic worms, shad colored crankbaits. Crappie are good in brush piles in 20-25 feet of water on minnows or grubs.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Bass and crappie are good on minnows in 10 feet of water.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have been hit-or-miss. Largemouth are good up shallow early and late.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles 15-20 feet of water on minnows or jigs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Shad are spawning so bass can be caught along the banks on topwaters.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good near the dam and in 15-20 feet of water with swimbaits and Texas rigged worms. Crappie are good in deep water 15-25 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: The morning bass bite is good for the first of hours of the day then slows on buzz baits, frogs, and swimbaits around shallow grass. Black bass are in a summer pattern. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork was definitely moving into the steady summer pattern this week. We are still seeing great numbers of black crappie on lay downs and certain trees in 14-28 feet. You can also find black crappie on certain docks and bridges over the next few months. We have been seeing lots of small white crappie on brush piles but some bigger keepers showed up the last few days. Some summer time trees are also holding white crappie and that will also get better over the next few weeks.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass and white bass are good with spinnerbaits off rocks, especially when it it wind swept.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass are up shallow bitting. Crappie are on brush piles and biting on minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Trolling rattle traps over points is probably your best chance to get active bass to chase on Granbury.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are really starting to pattern on docks and structure using worms and grubs. Crappie are tight to structure in Luces Bayou and East Fork using hand tied jigs in 8-14 feet.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass can still be caught on topwaters in the morning, then on Carolina rigs later in the day on rocky points and ledges.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 15-25 feet of water on brush with minnows or jigs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are good with catches up to 8 pounds flipping into flooded bushes with creature baits. Bass are good on points and brush piles with jigs, Texas rigged worms, or dropshot.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: White bass are out on the main lake humps 30-40 feet deep with a chartreuse or white slab 1-2 ounce slab with a jig tied 18 inches above for a two banger. Crappie remain slow while the floodgates are open but can be found roaming or on structure in 7-18 feet.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 15-20 feet of water with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: The crappie are stacked up in 6012 feet this week on brush piles and standing timber. Largemouth bass are still in 3 feet or less on Texas rigs, frogs, and jackhammer chatterbaits. Some largemouth bass have also moved back to the main lake brush, bulkheads, docks in 4-8 feet using Texas rig, and jackhammer chatterbaits for the deeper bass.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: 5-12 feet of water using slabs.
reports.by: Michael Richardson, Lake Livingston Adventures

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good fishing the hydrilla with senkos and redbug worms Texas rigged. Crappie are good at railroad trestle and deep brush using minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on Carolina rigs, dropshots and deep diving crankbaits. Crappie are fair on brush and some timber with chartreuse crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on dropshots and large swimbaits. Crappie are excellent on midlake standing timber live minnows.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 10 pounds on large worms Texas rigged and on shakey heads. Topwater bite is slowing down on big bass, but numbers are still good. Crappie fair.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in 6 feet of water.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park and Resort

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Bass are excellent on dropshot and big swimbaits. Crappie are slow on live minnows.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good and relating to brush 18-26 feet deep with some fish suspended mid depth minnows working best.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: White bass were biting live bait and slabs 30-55 feet of water on the banks at daylight day to day. Corp piles are starting to hold some crappie 20-30 feet hitting minnows or brighter jigs.
reports.by: Justin Wilson, Wilson Outdoor Connection

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on slabs on main lake points and humps in 25-35 feet of water.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in the flooded bushes and trees with soft plastics. Few bass are on points and creek Carolina rigs and crankbaits. Some crappie are shallow and some are roaming in open water. Crappie are best on brush in 12 feet of water, but while the lake level is high the brush piles are 16-18 feet deep. Bass are shallow in flooded bushes and trees in 4-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: Catfish, and bluegill are fair while crappie are good on minnows, worms, and stink bait at Somerville Marina early morning. Black bass are fair hitting soft crankbaits and spinnerbaits in 6-10 feet of water. Crappie good on the brush piles in 10-20 feet of water and pilings biting minnows and small jigs.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good at the crappie house. Largemouth bass are in similar areas as the crappie hitting the crappie jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on jigs and live minnows on structure and docks in 15-20 feet of water. Slow lift and sometimes adding a crappie nibble fish are hitting suspended through the brush. Bass are fair on top waters early on points and in the backs of coves at daylight. The topwater and slab bite should begin and be the way to go for the summer.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 1-15 feet of water hitting just about how ever you like to fish, from top water frog, spinnerbait, chatterbait, anything around the flooded bushes. Crappie fishing has been just ok, with the water still fallen and still getting these bugs storms, it is really needed to calm down before it really helps.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair with mostly bigger fish over numbers in the marinas with shad imitation topwaters, swimbaits or jerkbaits. There is a very slow bass bite on dropshots or craws fishing very slowly on bluff walls or points. Lake Travis is continuing to produce bass.
reports.by: Randal Frisbie, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: The bass are good all over the lake on crankbaits, topwaters, and trick worms. Crappie are good in 16 feet of water on the brush piles.
reports.by: Paul Taylor, The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with numbers being caught mainly on worms, but a swimbait, moving baits like crankbaits, wakebaits and spinnerbaits are working as well when there is a good amount of bait in the water. Bass are good with a top water bite early in the morning until the clouds burn off. The shell cracker, crappie and panfish anglers all seem to be catching good numbers. Bass fishing has been good, averaging around 30 a trip using worms in the grass.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on main lake brush piles on minnows and jigs. Bass are slow on deeper water drop-offs with crankbaits, and chatterbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 15-25 feet of water on minnows.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black Bass are fair in 15-30 feet of water on points and near deep water access, using Texas rigged Senko in green pumpkin, watermelon red, pumpkinseed, red bug colors. Crappie are also fair using crappie jigs and light line with small spoons.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arrowhead fishing report
reports.text: Most of the crappie have finished spawning, transitioning to deeper water for the summer pattern, but some can be caught shallow.
reports.by: Brandon Brown, Brown’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair, catching scattered fish on grass edges out to 12 feet with shaky head worms and jigs. Crappie have slowed down on brush with small jigs working best.
reports.by: Jim Brack, Athens Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been good on flukes and swimbaits in shad or bluegill colors. Report by Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop. Bass are schooling early morning in the discharge, with some action on the main lake afterwards.
reports.by: Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in brush piles 20-25 feet with minnows or jigs. Bass are good on shallow points chasing the shad spawn with Texas rig worms, crankbaits, chatterbaits, spinnerbaits, or flipping into flooded bushes. Black bass are slow on streamers and clousers fishing main lake points and flooded grass.
reports.by: Mike Stroman, R & R Marine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Catfish are being caught around rock and reed lines with cheese bait and cut shad bass are still being caught in the reeds.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing continues to be outstanding! Live bait and slabs have been putting them in the boat. Largemouth bass have been good on topwater baits early.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 6.41 pounds are slow on jigs, shaky heads and top waters in 2-10 feet of water. Crappie to 11 inches are fair under docks with black and chartreuse or white with a chartreuse head jigs in 9 feet of water, and on brush piles with minnows in 12 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass top water bite is starting to heat up with frogs, buzz baits and choppos plus pop r’s are working as the brim are starting to bed up.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Blue catfish are being caught out on the lake on rock piles and drop offs using cut bait bass are slow.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: The largemouth bass have really been doing good this week hitting top water.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are doing well on offshore structure and bream beds. Crappie are in 12-21 feet of water around structure and timber using plastics, hair or minnows, it’s been a light bite here lately.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles 15-20 feet of water on minnows or jigs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are good on fishing the boat docks, and shallow points chasing the shad spawn with Texas rig worms, crankbaits, chatterbaits, spinnerbaits, or flipping into flooded bushes.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good on main lake structures with slabs with teaser flies. Crappie are fair to good on brush piles and main lake structure on jigs with white color combos.
reports.by: Chad Ferguson of North Texas Catfish Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good along the dam and in deep water with Carolina rigs, shaky head, or trick worms. Crappie are good in deep water 15-25 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are improving to good early morning on topwaters around flooded grass and weeds, an frogs working over pond weed. Black bass are in a summer pattern. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork was definitely moving into the steady summer pattern this week. We are still seeing great numbers of black crappie on lay downs and certain trees in 14-28 feet. You can also find black crappie on certain docks and bridges over the next few months. We have been seeing lots of small white crappie on brush piles but some bigger keepers showed up the last few days. Some summer time trees are also holding white crappie and that will also get better over the next few weeks.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie is a little slower because of the muddy water. Bass fishing is good up shallow in the new vegetation in the water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass continue to be good on slabs on feeding flats early and late. Largemouth bass are fair to good on crankbaits and soft plastics worked near creek entrances. Some good topwater action for largemouth bass is possible near main lake points. Crappie are moving to their post spawn locations on structure and are good to excellent on small jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on spinnerbaits fished in shallow cover. Crappie are good on jigs fished over cover in 12-18 feet of water. White bass are fair on slab spoons fishing windy points and roadbeds.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are challenging around grass and brush. Bead heads will tempt bream and bass.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are hitting in the back lakes off the main channel on frogs and dark worms. Crappie are north in 8-14 feet of water being caught around structure with small hand tied jigs.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston County fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are hitting square bill crankbaits or shaken heads on docks, and swim jigs in shallow water around vegetation. Crappie are on minnows around standing timber and offshore brush in 8-14 feet.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting soft plastics in brush piles at midrange depths.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 15-20 feet of water with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good grass beds and bulkheads with swimbaits, shallow crankbaits, wake baits and flukes.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair to good on humps and points in 20-35 feet of water with slabs, jigs, and live bait. Crappie are fair in 4-25 feet of water. Bass are in 4-10 feet of water with crankbaits, spinnerbaits or dragging a soft plastic.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 8-17 feet of water on brush piles, standing timber and power lines using minnows. Largemouth bass are still in 3 feet or less on Texas rigs, frogs, and jackhammer chatterbaits. Some largemouth bass have also moved back to the main lake brush, bulkheads, docks in 4-8 feet using Texas rig, and jackhammer chatterbaits for the deeper bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Fishing duck tracker slabs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow on senkos worked slowly over the hydrilla, or deep crankbaits in deeper water. Crappie remain good over brush in 20-25 feet using minnows and blue and green Bobby Garland jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on topwater frogs, Carolina rigs, dropshots and medium diving crankbaits. Bass are consistently 3-6 pounds. Crappie are good on brush chartreuse and white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on Carolina rigs, dropshots or deep diving crankbaits. Bass are consistently 3-6 pounds. Crappie are excellent on midlake timber with chartreuse and white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has been good on white chatterbait or spinnerbaits early morning and evening. Midday flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-3 feet of water is the ticket to catch shaded up largemouth bass. Crappie were good around boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around river channel bends.
