reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good with catches up to 9 pounds on topwaters shallow early in the mornings then good on 10 inch worms, Hags F6.5 and F8, Rage MagCutters in PlumApple, redbug and green pumpkin off ledges and deeper timber later in the day. Crappie slow and scattered in big timber on minnows.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been very good, with soft plastics working well at the flooded edges, shallow crankbaits and small spinners in the shallows.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite has slowed down, due to the rising water. Bass are improving.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park and Resort

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Bass are excellent on a topwater spook or frog. Bass are consistently 2-5 pounds. Crappie are poor on timber with natural colored crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Use live shad or small slabs and jigs white, and silver are good colors. Bass are good early in the morning with topwater lures. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide Service.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Proctor fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and shad have been a little scarce.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: White bass are excellent relating to humps and long points in 17-26 feet of water using 3/4 ounce Bovee slab with a jig 12 inches above. Crappie are good and relating to brush 18-26 feet deep with some fish suspended mid depth.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are scattered in 15-25 feet of water with minnows.
reports.by: Justin Wilson, Wilson Outdoor Connection

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good with slabs on main lake points and humps in 25-35 feet of water. Crappie fair on minnows over brush piles in 15-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Lots of freshwater with bass in the brush and trees. Bass on humps and pockets Carolina rigs and big crankbaits. Crappie are moving around a lot because of the freshwater.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: Catfish, crappie and bluegill are good on minnows, worms, and stink bait at Somerville Marina early morning. Black Bass are fair hitting soft crankbaits and spinnerbaits in 6-10 feet of water. Crappie good on the brush piles in 10-20 feet of water and pilings biting minnows and small jigs.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Fishing for largemouth bass in the newly flooded terrestrial vegetation and along the inside edge of what was the shallowest hydrilla stands has been excellent for quality fish on soft plastics, including sunfish imitating soft plastics.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: The crappie bite is also good. The largemouth bass bite is fair.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texana fishing report
reports.text: Bass and bass are fair north of the U.S.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair using top waters early along the bluffs and on long points. Crappie are fair using jigs fishing structure using electronics to locate active fish in 12-18 feet of water.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 1-20 feet of water hitting your favorite way to fish. There was a big bass tournament this past weekend and there was four bass over 10 pounds caught. The crappie fishing is just fair due to the current running in the lake. There are some crappie shallow, around docks, but most are running from 12-18 feet.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are still scattered and slow.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: The bass are good on crankbaits, topwaters, and trick worms. Crappie are in 16 feet of waters on the brush piles.
reports.by: Paul Taylor, The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Anglers are catching crappie, blue catfish, channel catfish, yellow catfish, white bass, hybrids, stripers and largemouth bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Bass are great with fish coming on four and five inch stick worms, craw worms and small swimbaits around the grass in 5-10 feet off the reeds. Some nice bass are coming out further throwing deep crankbaits and jerkbaits in shad colors.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow. Crappie are fair on main lake brush piles on minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good in shallow water main lake points and fish are reported being caught on main lake structure on slabs. White bass are good on main lake structures on slabs with teaser flies. Crappie are fair to good on brush piles and main lake structure on jigs with white color combos.
reports.by: Chad Ferguson of North Texas Catfish Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good and still favor brush and points.
reports.by: Jerry Gennings, local angler and guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good shallow to 18 feet of water on jigs and minnows. Bass are still on beds.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on main lake points in 10-20 feet off chunk rock with Texas rigged senkos, Ned rigs, and shaky heads.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arrowhead fishing report
reports.text: The crappie are still biting, but have slowed compared to weeks prior. Female crappie are still being caught with eggs, but a majority have spawned. Crappie are transitioning to the summer patterns on brush piles, and docks with shade.
reports.by: Brandon Brown, Brown’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has been decent, but not as good as previous weeks.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good using shad or bluegill colored flukes and swimbaits. Report by Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop. Bass are schooling early in the morning in the discharge and out over grass flats on the opposite end of the lake as well.
reports.by: Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in brush piles 20-25 feet with minnows or jigs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are good on shallow points chasing the shad spawn with Texas rig worms, crankbaits, chatterbaits, spinnerbaits, or flipping into flooded bushes. Bead heads and clousers should work well for bass around retaining walls and boat docks. Look for crappie around brush and shallow banks, small wooly buggers are excellent.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brady fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow with a few catches on spinnerbaits along rocky shoreline and brush. Crappie are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 5.79 pounds are good on chatterbaits, shakyhead and crankbaits in 3-12 feet of water. Crappie are good with catches up to 13 inches under docks in 5-9 feet of water with black and chartreuse, or white with a chartreuse head jig in 5-9 feet of water. Some crappie are on brush piles using minnows in 10-12 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: You can still find bass on trees with senkos and flukes.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Use spinnerbaits like a mepps#4 spinner or drop a slab down to the bottom and work it fast up and down and the fish will hit it immediately. Also throwing out a slab and reeling it back with a slow retrieve is also working well. The crappie bite has been getting increasingly better.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on Model A Bomber crankbaits, and crappie are good on minnows in 15-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are in 10-17 feet of water near structure using crankbaits, jerkbaits, as well as worms. Hybrids are in 17-28 feet of water on flats or humps jigging slabs, swimbaits or minnows and shad. Crappie are in 12-21 feet of water around structure and timber biting plastics, hair or minnows.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Corpus Christi Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow. Largemouth bass are slow.
reports.by: Captain Damian Hubbs, Top Gun Outfitters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on fishing the boat docks, and shallow points chasing the shad spawn with Texas rig worms, crankbaits, chatterbaits, spinnerbaits, or flipping into flooded bushes.
reports.by: Mike Stroman, R & R Marine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Bass are excellent with numbers being caught in 15-20 feet of water casting to shallow rocky areas with deep diving crankbaits, football jigs, and dropshots. Crappie are slow.
reports.by: Ram Reyes, Ram Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has improved this week. Black bass are in a post spawn pattern and aggressive. Crappies are shallow catching them on the edge of banks, small fish patterns like wooly buggers are a good bet. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork is finally beginning to settle into its post spawn summer pattern. Black crappie are loading up on certain trees, brush piles and lay downs in huge numbers. White crappie should be loading up on their post spawn patterns over the next few weeks.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on brush and biting. Bass are biting good up shallow in the new submerged grass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass fishing continues to be good to excellent on slabs and spinnerbaits when located. Largemouth bass are fair to good with catches up to 7 pounds fishing crankbaits and soft plastics near docks and creek entrances where the water is clearer. Largemouth bass are good from the banks, hitting medium sized minnows. Sand bass are slow with a light bite on slabs. Crappie are schooling through lake.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on spinnerbaits fished in shallow cover. Crappie are good on jigs fished over cover in 12-18 feet of water. White bass are fair on slab spoons fished on windy points and roadbeds.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are rebounding quickly eating hand tied jigs and small plastics in 8-14 feet of water tight to structure. Largemouth have recovered the fastest with reports of several big bass being caught on grubs and worms by docks and structure.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston County fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in deep water brush piles, standing timber and power lines in 12-15 feet of water with minnows. Largemouth bass are good in 1-7 feet of water with frogs, wacky worms, weightless Texas rigs, yum dingers or swim jigs.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting crankbaits, soft plastics from the bank to 14 feet on ledges and drop-offs with Carolina rigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be found shallow in the flooded brush caught with your favorite soft plastic. Crappie are on the brush piles and in the grass edges on minnows or crappie jigs.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 15-25 feet of water on brush with minnows or jigs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are good with catches up to 8 pounds flipping into flooded bushes with creature baits.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Use 1 ounce or 2 ounce slabs in white or chartreuse with a jig tied about 18 inches above it for a double. Crappie are slow. Black bass are loving the newly flooded brush and forest.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 20 feet of water on brush piles with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in deep brush piles, standing timber and power lines in 13-17 feet of water biting minnows. Largemouth bass are good in 1-4 feet of water in the creek channels using topwater frogs, swim jigs, Texas rigs, spinnerbaits, and chatterbaits.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair to good on Ribbit frogs, swimbaits and redbug worms over the hydrilla. Crappie are good in 25-30 feet of water at the top of brush with minnows and power bait minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with good numbers of 2-4 pound fish being caught in shallow vegetation with topwater frogs and spooks, or swim jigs. Crappie are excellent on brush and standing timber with chartreuse crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent with good numbers on Carolina rigs, dropshots or deep crankbaits in 12-15 feet of water. Crappie are good with live shiners or natural colored crappie jigs roaming in schools in the middle of the water column.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Reports of a nice size largemouth bass caught from the shore by a young angler.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on topwaters with catches up to 7 pounds. Crappie are fair, migrating toward deeper trees suspended 10-12 feet.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been up in the flooded grass and under tree branches in the water hitting frogs and soft jerkbaits, or squarebill crankbaits fished in front. Crappie reports remain the same, good in deep water, 16-24 feet, when you can get out there, scattered shallow bite early morning and again evening.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good in numbers of 3-5 pound fish in 18 feet of water with Carolina rigs, dropshot, soft plastic trick worms. Black crappie are fair in the east arm of the lake with natural colored crappie jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are slow, use live shad or small slabs and jigs. Fishing conditions are the same with a few bass in shallow water but transitioning deeper. Bass are good on topwaters in the mornings, then using worms later in the day in 12-15 feet of water. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide Service.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: White bass relating to humps, levees and long points in 17-29 feet of water using 3/4 ounce Bovee slab with a jig 12 inches above. Crappie are good, relating to brush in 14-18 feet using minnows and jigs.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie is good 15-20 foot of water, brush piles.
reports.by: Justin Wilson, Wilson Outdoor Connection

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good with slabs on main lake points and humps in 25-35 feet of water.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair with catches up to 7 pounds possible on points and deeper water with Carolina or Texas rigs. The frog bite is picking up bass in shallow lily pads and brush. Crappie are good on brush piles, minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: Catfish and crappie fair and bluegill good on minnows, worms, and stink bait at Somerville Marina early morning. Black Bass are fair hitting soft crankbaits and spinnerbaits in 6-10 feet of water. Crappie good on the brush piles in 10-20 feet of water and pilings biting minnows and small jigs.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in shallow water with crappie jigs. Largemouth bass are in similar areas as the crappie hitting the crappie jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: With flooded terrestrial vegetation now around the entire perimeter of the lake, largemouth bass are now scattered both in that brush, and in the shallower hydrilla.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Artificial lures, such as slabs are working good and so is live bait. Crappie are good on minnows in 10-15 feet on brush piles and bridge columns. The largemouth bite is great in 1-5 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is good using live shad and top waters along the bluffs and dam wall in the clear water. Crappie fishing is good on brush piles in 12-18 feet of water using jigs and live minnows catching them suspended around the structure and boat docks.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are very active with numbers being caught in open water schools with swimbaits and jerkbaits. Bass are on the verge of schooling action with fish feeding shallow along the bank and up in the water column off shore and around marinas.
reports.by: Randal Frisbie, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair in all depths on crankbaits, spinnerbaits, and trick worms. Crappie are fair, scattered in 16 feet of water with minnows.
reports.by: Paul Taylor, The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: A few reports of catches of crappie, white bass, largemouth bass and blue catfish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Big groups of shad in the back of many coves, but bass are not blasting them. Bass are spread out between the reeds, grass, with bigger fish are biting on the deeper edges of grass, but there are not as many bites. Crappie bite is good in deeper brush tops, and in the grass. Crappie are good in 5-10 feet of water with black and chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good with the best bite on stick worms, but a small swimbait or jerkbait is getting some of the bigger fish. Bass are chasing big baitfish schools all around the lake.
reports.by: David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair with mostly smaller sized fish being caught on deeper water brush piles with minnows or jigs. Bass are slow in transition deeper to the summer pattern depths hitting crankbaits and chatterbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair using minnows on brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and bass can be caught in spawn and post spawn patterns in 1-15 feet of water.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on the main lake and secondary points.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arrowhead fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are very good near the state park and around the bridges, with some moving out to brush.
reports.by: Brandon Brown, Brown’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair working the outside edges of grass with jigs and shaky-head worms. Schooling bass are starting to fire up. Crappie are good on small jigs and minnows on brush piles out to 30 feet.
reports.by: Jim Brack, Athens Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are very active in the morning and evening. Bass are good using chatterbaits and spinnerbaits fished over grass and around shoreline cover are good.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good using shad or bluegill colored flukes and swimbaits. Report by Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop. Some bass are near creek mouths and a little ways in, most are along grass lines on the main lake.
reports.by: Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in brush piles 20-25 feet with minnows or jigs. Catfish are excellent in 2-6 feet of water in flooded brush with worms, cut bait cheese bait. and bass are good at Blow Hole using chrome rattle traps. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are good on shallow points chasing the shad spawn with Texas rig worms, crankbaits, chatterbaits, spinnerbaits, or flipping into flooded bushes. Bead heads and clousers should work well for bass around retaining walls and boat docks. Look for crappie around brush and shallow banks, small wooly buggers are excellent.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brady fishing report
reports.text: Black bass and crappie are slow after the spawn, should pick up soon due to bluegill spawn.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in the reeds on plastic worms.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to be hot, especially from the mid lake area south. Topwater baits and slabs have been putting them in the boat. Largemouth bass have been good on topwaters, flat billed crankbaits, finesse baits.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 9.65 pounds are good on wacky rigs, shaky head and crankbaits in 3-12 feet of water. Crappie up to 13 inches are good along the shoreline with black and chartreuse, or white with chartreuse head jigs out to 4 feet of water. Crappie are good with minnows on brush piles in 10-12 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Lake is high and the bass bite is tough. Bass are suspended on piles and near the dam. The water levels are high, but anglers are reporting catches of catfish, crappie and bass.
reports.by: The Aggie Anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 15-20 feet of water with black and chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good in the backs of creeks, flip every stick up as there is still some spawning action.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass are holding extremely tight on trees while the water is falling and very slow to bite flukes, senkos and light Texas rigs.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the hydrilla with a chatterbait, and with a dropshot in deeper grass or main lake points.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Use spinner baits or drop a slab down to the bottom and work it fast up and down. The crappie bite has been increasingly better.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on shad colored moving baits in the morning on shallow flats. Bass are good in shallow water using crankbaits, or spinnerbaits. Crappie are good in 20-25 feet of water on minnows or grubs.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good hitting topwaters. Crappie are good on minnows.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Coleman fishing report
reports.text: Before the rise in water bass reports were good.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass have been good. Hybrids are in 17-28 feet of water on flats or humps, jigging slabs, swimbaits or minnows and shad. Crappie are in 11-21 feet around structure and timber using plastics, hair or minnows.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Corpus Christi Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth are very slow. Crappie are slow.
reports.by: Captain Damian Hubbs, Top Gun Outfitters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on shallow points chasing the shad spawn with Texas rig worms, crankbaits, chatterbaits, spinnerbaits, or flipping into flooded bushes.
reports.by: Mike Stroman, R & R Marine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair in shallow water along dam rocks with spinnerbaits and crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair early morning on topwaters and frogs around grass. Bass are good on shaky heads at the edge of grass in 3-5 feet, or Carolina rigs on points and secondary points in 5-8 feet. Black bass are in a post spawn pattern and aggressive. Crappies are shallow catching them on the edge of banks, small fish patterns like wooly buggers are a good bet. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork has been up and down this past week with the heavy rains and big winds. We are finally seeing some black crappie loading up on certain laydowns and docks. Seeing a few brush piles in certain areas loading up with white crappie. You can still find white crappie on timber in 10-18ft and we should see more…
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Crappie were biting shallow on jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Most bass and crappie are done spawning, transitioning back out to brush. Bass are good on plastics and crankbaits. Crappie are good on jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Granbury sand bass fishing continues to be good to excellent on chartreuse and white slabs fished in 12-20 feet of water from Decordova Subdivision to in town by the Shores. Crappie catches on small jigs and minnows are good on submerged structures and docks. Largemouth bass are fair to good on a variety of baits. Spinner baits, crankbaits and soft plastics are all producing bass to 6 pounds in the backs of sloughs and creeks. Sand bass are good jigging slabs while anchored or drifting, trolling Alabama rigs with 3 inch swimbaits or other soft plastics.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on topwaters fished in shallow water. Crappie are good on jigs fished over structure. White bass are fair on slab spoons fished along shallow roadbeds.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Greenbelt fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in shallow water on jigs and minnows. Largemouth bass are good on soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass and white bass will light up. Shortly after that the crappie will turn back on.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston County fishing report
reports.text: Crappie made a big move to deeper water brush piles, standing timber and power lines in 12-15 feet of water this week. Crappie can be caught on minnows. Largemouth bass frog bite has picked up. Largemouth bass are good in 1-7 feet of water with frogs, wacky worms, weightless Texas rigs, yum dingers or swim jigs.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing slowed on brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on dropshots, shaky heads, and Carolina rigs on offshore structure.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in standing timber across from the Alley Creek area in 25-30 feet of water with jigs or minnows. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are good with catches up to 8 pounds flipping into flooded bushes with creature baits.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are roaming and we are not seeing a lot of structure yet. White bass are on fire throwing topwaters, paddle tails, swimbaits, or using 1 ounce slabs with the jig, tied 18 inches above it. If the fish are blowing up on the shore and you do not want to throw lures at them, you can just drop down a slab in 14-15 feet of water just outside of them and turn your Bobo thumper to draw them under the boat.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair to good on humps and points in 20-35 feet of water with slabs, jigs and live bait. Crappie are fair using minnows or jigs in 4-25 feet of water on brush piles, rock piles, stumps, standing timber, and laydowns. Bass are in 4-10 feet of water with crankbaits, spinnerbaits or dragging a soft plastic.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie made a big move to deeper water brush piles, standing timber and power lines in 13-17 feet of water this week. Crappie can be caught on minnows. Largemouth bass frog bite has picked up. Largemouth bass are good on spawning beds in 1-4 feet of water in the creek channels using swim jigs, Texas rigs, spinnerbaits, and chatterbaits.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair fishing over the hydrilla with weightless senkos and wacky rigged worms. Crappie are good on deep brush in 25-30 feet of water using shad colored jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millers Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Blue catfish have been caught near the dam while anglers were targeting crappie with jigs. Crappie are fair in brush piles in 10 feet or more. Largemouth bass are slow, targeting recently submerged areas shallow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on 6 inch glide bait, dropshots, medium diving crankbait on offshore channel swings. Crappie are excellent on brush and standing timber with chartreuse crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Some bass have situated themselves near the roadbeds and some are starting to gather, suspended, over the deep creeks. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on topwater frogs, large ribbon tail soft plastics, and dropshots in 12-15 feet of water. Crappie are excellent using chartreuse jigs on brush and standing timber.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good with numbers of 4-9 pounds fish caught with a variety of swimming baits in shallow brush in 4 feet of water. Bigger bass are in 20 feet of water hitting crankbaits and 10 inch worms. Crappie are moving to bigger hardwood trees 8-19 feet with small red head jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on plastic creature baits and stick baits in watermelon purple swirl or green pumpkin, and squarebill crankbaits. Crappie bite is improving on crappie jigs.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good in numbers fishing the deep water on the south end near the dam with 6-8 inch flutter spoons, dropshot and spooks. Black crappie are fair on natural colored crappie jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are slow to fair with fish scattered in 10-20 feet of water using live shad or small slabs and jigs in white or silver. Fishing patterns are holding steady for bass. Bass are good on topwaters in the mornings, then using worms later in the day in 8-15 feet of water. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide Service.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on structure 15-20 feet on minnows.
reports.by: Justin Wilson, Wilson Outdoor Connection

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White Bass are good on main lake points and humps in 25-35 feet of water with a slab and jig combination.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are on points and deeper water with Carolina or Texas rigs. The frog bite is picking up bass in shallow lily pads and brush. Crappie are primarily on brush with a few shallow spawners in cypress trees. Target bass on grass, bushes and standing timber using topwater frogs, small swimbaits, and swim jigs.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: Catfish are fair and crappie and bluegill good on minnows, worms, and stink bait at Somerville Marina early morning. Black bass are slow hitting soft crankbaits and plastic baits in 5-8 feet of water. Crappie good on the brush piles in 10-20 feet of water and pilings biting minnows and small jigs.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Spence fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good flipping jigs or vibrating jigs into the shallows. Crappie are reported to be slow.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite is good when you can find spawning crappie in shallow water with crappie jigs. Largemouth bass are in similar areas as the crappie hitting the crappie jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing continues to be the main draw on this hydrilla-packed reservoir with most consistent anglers targeting fish on the deep outside edge of hydrilla beds.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texana fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair north of the U.S. Crappie are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is slow as most fish are shallow up in the trees and grass that is flooded after a few years of being dry. Slip corks with minnows in the trees, docks are producing a few on jigs with a crappie nibble tip. Smallmouth and largemouth bass are good on top waters and plastics along rocks where shad are spawning early. Tires near marinas will hold bass as well.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with lots of action on top water baits for the first hour of daylight. Crappie bite if off due to the high water and current.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the main lake in shallow water and pockets, and points off the main lake with swimbaits and craws. Bigger bass on craws, creature baits, with better numbers on dropshots. More bass are starting to show up in marinas. Expect the frog bite and topwater to turn on, and suspended shad under marinas makes for schooling bass as well. The majority of bass are done spawning, but you may stumble upon some along small pockets or ledges on the main lake in about as deep as you can see on bluff walls.
reports.by: Randal Frisbie, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow and scattered on brush in 7-8 feet of water, but as the water temperature increases water temperatures crappie should move to deeper water on brush. No reports of largemouth bass.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair in all depths on crankbaits, spinnerbaits, and trick worms. Crappie are fair in 16 feet of water on brush piles with minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Paul Taylor, The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Big groups of shad in the back of many coves, but bass are not blasting them. Bass are spread out between the reeds, grass, with bigger fish are biting on the deeper edges of grass, but there are not as many bites. Crappie bite is good in deeper brush tops, and in the grass. Crappie are good in 5-10 feet of water with black and chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair with smaller sized catches in deeper water brush piles with minnows or jigs. Bass are slow transitioning to summer pattern depths hitting crankbaits and chatterbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are loading up on brush tops all over the lake. Crappie are biting best on points with minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Jerry Gennings, local angler and guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair over brush in 5-15 feet of water on minnows.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on main lake points near deep water access, with the best fish coming in 10-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Target bass with moving baits on cover.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arrowhead fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing has been bery good at the state park, the fishing pier and the bridges.
reports.by: Brandon Brown, Brown’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow with shaky heads, Carolina rigs and jigs on the first breaks in 8-12 feet grass lines. Crappie are fair on brush piles in 25 feet of water with 3/32 ounce jigs in shad or chartreuse colors.
reports.by: Jim Brack, Athens Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early in the morning in shallow water using chatterbaits, spinnerbaits.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been good on flukes and swimbaits. Report by Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop. Some bass are near creek mouths and a little ways in, most are along grass lines on the main lake.
reports.by: Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: Fish the white, 5/8 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab vertically from a fixed position until the fish quit responding, then check side-imaging for fish to the side of your boat.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 15-20 feet of water on brush piles or downed timber on minnows or jigs. Catfish are good in shallow flooded brush with worms or cheese bait. and bass are good at Blow Hole using chrome rattle traps. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Flip into flooded bushes for bass. Bass are transitioning to the first breakline in 6-8 feet of water hitting Texas rig worms, crankbaits, chatterbaits, spinnerbaits. Look for crappie around brush and shallow banks, small wooly buggers are excellent.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are still in the weeds and along some rock lines using crankbaits and plastic worms.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have been spawning close to shore, especially in the southern end. Largemouth bass are mostly in a post spawn pattern.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 8.50 pounds are good on jigs, spinnerbaits and crankbaits in 3-12 feet of water. Crappie are good along the shoreline out to 4 feet with black and chartreuse and brush piles with minnows in 10-12 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Bass are suspended on piles and near the dam. Consistent fishing patterns for catfish, crappie and bass near the restaurant, off rocks and floating docks with small minnows, worms, and cut bait.
reports.by: The Aggie Anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: The bass will still be holding tight on the trees with the water falling quickly but hopefully the grass fish will turn on soon. Fish in the river where bass will group up after the spawn in the river hitting dropshots, shaky heads or Texas rigs.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Reports of great catches using silver or white slabs and spinners and retrieving off the bottom at a very slow retrieve to catch these fish in depths of 8-16 feet of water. The crappie have also migrated back into the main lake.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bass are excellent using imitation shad in the morning, then switching to Carolina or Texas rigs on main lakes points as the day progresses. Bass are good in shallow water using crankbaits, or spinnerbaits. Crappie are good in 20-25 feet of water on minnows or grubs.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 10 feet of water on minnows. Lots of bass are jumping chasing minnows on the surface.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Coleman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on jigs at the docks and should be moving back to brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good with some still on spawning beds. Hybrids are in 17-28.feet of water using jigging slabs, swimbaits, minnows or shad. Crappie bite can be tough but is improving in 11-21 feet of water using plastics, hair jigs or minnows.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Flip into flooded bushes for bass. Bass are scattered on the first break line with crankbaits. Early in the morning shad are spawning and bass are chasing shallow.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: The crappie fishing on Lake Fork has been great this week if you find the right areas and patterns to fish. The spawn is coming to an end and the black crappie are beginning to load up on certain bridges and docks. If you search you can find some big schools of keeper size black crappie. You can still find some larger white crappie on timber in 10-22ft. Also seeing some white crappie loading up on certain brush in some areas close to where they spawned.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Granbury sand bass fishing continues to be good to excellent on chartreuse and white slabs fished in 12-20 feet of water from Decordova Subdivision to in town by the Shores. Crappie catches on small jigs and minnows are good on submerged structures and docks. Largemouth bass are fair to good on a variety of baits. Spinner baits, crankbaits and soft plastics are all producing bass to 6 pounds in the backs of sloughs and creeks. Sand bass can be caught with live bait or slabs bounced off the bottom on shallow flats and ledges on the south end.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on spinnerbaits and topwaters in shallow cover. Crappie are good on jigs fished over brush in 6 to 12 feet of water.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Greenbelt fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in shallow water on jigs and minnows. Largemouth bass are spawning biting soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are hanging tight to structure being caught on worms and grubs. Crappie are tight to structure in 8-14 feet of water being caught on snap jigs.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston County fishing report
reports.text: Crappie, largemouth bass and catfish are still on beds. White bass are good early in 10 feet of water then in 17 feet of water in the afternoon with chartreuse or silver slabs. Largemouth bass are good in 1-7 feet of water with frogs, wacky worms, weightless Texas rigs, yum dingers or swim jigs. Crappie are in 10 feet or less using minnows on standing timber, brush, or deep docks.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in 10 feet of water hitting crankbaits, shaky heads spinnerbaits and Carolina rigs. Crappie are on brush piles hitting minnows or jigs. Report by Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding.
reports.by: Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting crankbaits, Carolina rigs, Texas rigged soft plastics, and frogs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are being caught over brush piles and at the edge of the hydrilla on crappie jigs. Bass, a few big ones can still be caught shallow with some moving out a little towards summer spots. Small bass are being caught up shallow on your favorite soft plastics.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 15-20 feet of water on brush with minnows or jigs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing. Flip into flooded bushes for bass. Bass are good in flooded bushes with creature baits.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 10-20 feet of water on brush piles with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good flipping docks with wacky rigged stick worms, jigs and flukes.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Smaller sandies are abundant using slabs, jigs, and live baits. Crappie are fair using minnows or jigs in 4-25 feet of water on brush piles, rock piles, stumps, standing timber, and laydowns.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie, largemouth bass and catfish are still on beds. Largemouth bass are good on spawning beds in 1-4 feet of water in the creek channels using swim jigs, Texas rigs, spinnerbaits, and chatterbaits. Crappie are good fishing minnows in brush, standing timber, and creek channels in 1-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair along the edge of the hydrilla using senkos with gold flake and Texas rigged redbug trick worms. Crappie are excellent in brush piles in 20-25 feet and at railroad trestle using minnows and Bobby Garland jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on minnows and artificials. Crappie are fair with artificial baits and minnows.
reports.by: Kenneth Wysong, SharKens Honey Hole

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on white chatterbaits flipping soft plastics in the reeds in 1-3 feet of water. Crappie are good around boat docks on chartreuse jigs.
reports.by: the Angelo State Fishing Team

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair to 10 pounds on various chatterbaits, topwaters and soft plastics in 12 feet of water or less. Crappie are fair on jigs and minnows around hardwood trees in 8-18 feet in The Colorado River.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow now that the females have laid eggs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: They are scattered in 10-20 feet of water using live shad or small slabs and jigs in white or silver. Bass are good on topwaters in the mornings, then using worms later in the day in 8-15 feet of water. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide Service.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Proctor fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass can be caught on soft plastics. Crappie are good in shallow and deep water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught casting weightless flukes into vegetation. Crappie can be caught with crappie jigs with live minnows and crappie bites.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: White bass relating to humps and long points in 17-26 feet of water using 3/4 ounce Bovee slab with a jig 12 inches above. Crappie are fair in 14-18 feet of water relating to brush.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Then fish in 25-35 feet of water later in the day with slabs. Crappie are good in 10-20 feet of water on minnows or blue and white jigs.
reports.by: Justin Wilson, Wilson Outdoor Connection

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good on main lake points and humps in 20-25 feet of water with a slab and jig combination. Crappie spawn is nearing an end, but reports still coming in on catches from shallow water on minnows.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in 8 feet or less with some in the lily pads on topwater frogs, or with Carolina rigs and jigs on harder bottoms and structures off points and humps. Crappie are transitioning to brush piles using minnows and jigs. Bass are good keying on hard clay points, grass edges and flooded timber with swim jigs, chatterbaits, topwater spooks or pop-r’s. Crappie have finished spawning in 12-20 feet of water on brush piles and standing timber.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: Catfish and crappie are fair and bluegill good on minnows, worms, and stink bait at Somerville Marina early morning. Black Bass are fair hitting soft crankbaits and plastic baits in 5-8 feet of water. Crappie good on the brush piles in 10-20 feet of water and pilings biting minnows and small jigs.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are scattered and the bite is slow. White bass are slow in 7 feet of water with bigger crappie jigs or minnows. Crappie are slow with many smaller sized catches.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Fish the white, 5/8 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab vertically from a fixed position until the fish quit responding, then check side-imaging for fish to the side of your boat. Largemouth bass fishing continues to be excellent with reports of frog fishing in the flooded shoreline terrestrial vegetation, and reports of weightless worm fishing over top of the newly flooded hydrilla.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Fish are being caught on humps and points in 15-25 feet on slabs and swimbaits. Crappie are good around docks and shallow brush. Largemouth bass are solid and biting good around lily pads, shallow docks, rip rap and concrete structure.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is good near boat docks and on structure also using electronics to locate roaming fish in 12-15 feet of water. Glo and milk are colors of choice with a crappie nibble tip. Bass fishing is good using top waters early, spooks or closed face glide baits and fish crawl baits later.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: There is a shad spawn going on in the morning and some afternoons attracting the bass. Bass are good on spinnerbaits, chatterbaits and small swimbaits. On an overcast day, bass can be caught on topwaters and frogs all day long. Crappie are fair on brush piles and deeper docks using 1/16 ounce jigs with a white or smoke color grub and live bait. Best area has been away from the big flow in the creeks, as crappie do not like the rushing water.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the main lake in shallow water and pockets, and points off the main lake with swimbaits and craws. Bigger bass on craws, creature baits, with better numbers on dropshots. More bass are starting to show up in marinas. The majority of bass are done spawning, but you may stumble upon some along small pockets or ledges on the main lake in about as deep as you can see on bluff walls.
reports.by: Randal Frisbie, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair but should improve in heavy cover in 8-12 feet of water with jigs or live minnows. Largemouth bass are fair on soft plastics and some topwaters.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair in 10 feet of water on crankbaits, spinnerbaits, and trick worms. Crappie are fair with many undersized catches scattered from the shallows to 20 feet of water on brush piles with minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Paul Taylor, The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with several 5-6.5 pound catches using a variety or lures but the lure of choice continues to be worms. Crappie anglers are catching good numbers. Lake Decker is going strong with better bass showing back up anywhere in or near the deeper grass lines. Be sure to flip into the edge of reeds as you can pull some big bass out.
reports.by: David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in deeper water brush piles with minnows or jigs. Primarily smaller sized crappie with a few keepers. Bass are slow transitioning to summer pattern depths hitting crankbaits and chatterbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good using minnows in the shallows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie spawn is over and fish are moving to the edges of deeper water on stumps and brush.
reports.by: Jerry Gennings, local angler and guide
